opening.headline: It explains what happens under the hood when repetitive tasks are handed over to agents, in terms of planning, tool calls, and human intervention.
body: Imagine having an agent create the same report every week, and seeing the results, but not being able to see what material was read or what was changed. If you don't know the inner workings, you can't set standards for how much to leave and where to let people look.

In this lesson, you'll learn what a workspace agent is and how it iterates over the process of creating a plan, calling a tool, and checking the results. Next, we look at the three points where human intervention occurs, and divide the steps to be taken by an agent and the steps taken by a person, as an example of monthly settlement reporting.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain how workspace agents work
You can distinguish between steps to be handled by agents and steps to be handled by humans.

screens.title: I've been assigned repetitive tasks, but I don't know what's going on inside.
screens.lead: First, read the situation of the person in charge of entrusting the work to the agent.

visual.alt: An illustration of a box where a request is entered and only results are released, and a person in charge who is worried because he cannot figure out what is inside.
labels: Create a settlement report every week
What materials did you read and what did you change?

paragraphs: A person in charge entrusted the weekly settlement report to a workspace agent. Results come out on time. However, you cannot tell what file the agent read, what numbers it changed, or where it got stuck just by looking at the results.

In this situation, it is difficult to determine the scope of entrustment. It makes me anxious to believe everything, and there is no point in trusting it to check everything again. We need standards for how much to leave and where to let people look at it.
Baselines can be established by knowing how agents work. In this class, we will see the order in which an agent carries out tasks and find a place for people in the process.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: What would be lost if you think of an agent's job as 'answer once and you're done'? I'll think about it again after seeing how it actually goes in class.

screens.outro: First, let's think about your repetitive tasks.

screens.title: Among repetitive tasks, which part does a person keep making the same judgment about?
screens.lead: If you first think about each question in your head and then select it, the instructor will organize your thoughts. You will not enter or submit an answer.

items.prompt: When collecting data, what tasks do you repeat the same every time?
items.answer: There are clear rules for finding and opening files in a given folder and moving them to the same format. These are tasks that agents are good candidates for calling tools to handle.

items.prompt: Do you apply the same criteria every time when organizing things into format?
items.answer: There are also fixed standards for calculating totals for each item and organizing them in a table. If the standards can be written down, I can leave it to you. On the other hand, if it is difficult to write down the standards, it is still too early to leave it to them.

items.prompt: The moment I check the final number, am I deciding to 'pass this and stop this'?
items.answer: That judgment is the signal that tells the person which section to take charge of. If you are responsible for the numbers or if it is difficult to roll back once distributed, it is better to leave a space for people to check right before doing so.

screens.outro: Now let's start by looking at what a workspace agent is.

screens.title: What is a Workspace Agent?
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn what a workspace agent is, how to create one, and what access rights it has.

tabs.label: something
tabs.body: ChatGPT Workspace Agent is an agent created for repetitive tasks and workflows. You can share the agents you create with team members or workspaces, use them in Slack, run them on a schedule, and have them run through APIs. You can also choose your model and inference strength, and connect to apps and tools. Gemini Enterprise also has agents created by employees using Workflow Builder, so the flow of creating and managing agents within an organization is common.

tabs.label: Where to find it
tabs.body: When you select Agents in the left sidebar of ChatGPT, three sections appear. Recently used shows recently used agents, Built by me shows agents I created, and Team directory shows agents created by the organization. When assigning repetitive work, first check the Team directory to see if there are already agents doing the same work.

tabs.label: How to make it
tabs.body: There are two ways to make it. When creating a template, select a template from Browse templates, select Use template, select a tool, and select Create Agent. When creating with the builder, select Create and enter what you want to do or select Start blank. Once you have a draft plan, review it, edit it, and then select Build this agent. Before creating, you can check the behavior and results with sample requests in Preview.

tabs.label: who can write
tabs.body: Workspace Agent is turned off by default in Enterprise workspaces, and is turned on by administrators for eligible workspaces. Role-based access control is enforced so users can only view and run agents they are authorized to access. The scope of sharing is set between 'Only me', 'Organization members with link', and 'Publish to organization directory'.

screens.outro: Now that we know what an agent is, let's look at the internal order of how things get done.

screens.title: Repeat planning, calling tools, and checking results
screens.lead: Select the arrows to follow the agent step by step as he or she completes a task.

visual.alt: A circular diagram of planning, calling tools, and checking results in a circular manner.

steps.title: work plan
steps.body: When an agent receives a goal, it first divides it into steps. When creating a workspace agent, the builder presents a draft plan and lets people make changes. The plan becomes the basis for all subsequent steps.

steps.title: tool call
steps.body: At each stage of the plan, agents invoke tools such as connected apps, files, and search to obtain information or take action. What an agent can read and write is limited to the human decisions made when establishing tool and app connections.

steps.title: Check results
steps.body: By looking at the results returned by the tool, the agent checks whether the plan is going well. If the file format is different or the value is empty, modify the plan and go to the next step. It is characteristic of an agent to repeat plans, tools, and results multiple times rather than answering once.

steps.title: Stop and check if necessary
steps.body: ChatGPT's agent method stops and prompts the user when confirmation or login is required. A person may change direction or interrupt a task midway. We have safeguards in place to ensure user verification for high-impact actions.

steps.title: For long tasks, go to Work.
steps.body: ChatGPT's Work is described as an agent for long, multi-step tasks and completed results. Quick conversations are handled in Chat, and multi-step tasks are assigned to Work. Usage depends on the type of task.

screens.outro: Now that we know the iteration structure, let's check the logs to see where people fit into this process.

screens.title: Where does human intervention come in?
screens.lead: When you select a highlighted passage in the example run log below, an explanation will appear. Find out where human intervention occurs. This record is an example for illustrative purposes.

data.text:
1. Objective verification: Prepare the settlement report from last month.  
2. Develop a plan: Collect files, calculate totals, mark abnormal amounts, and write a draft.  
3. Call the tool: Read three settlement files from the connected drive.  
4. Check the result: Correct the plan because the format of one file is different.  
5. Confirmation request: Login is required and waits for a response from the user.  
6. Draft completion: Create the report draft and indicate two unusual amounts.  
7. Delivery: A person checks the final numbers and distributes them.

marks.span: Develop a plan: Collect files, calculate totals, mark abnormal amounts, and write a draft.
marks.note: This is the result of a pre-start intervention. The goal, tools to be used, and scope of approach are determined in advance by the person. During the planning phase, agents' draft plans can be reviewed and modified by humans.

marks.span: Call the tool: Read three settlement files from the connected drive.
marks.note: Tool calls only occur within the app the person is connected to and within the permitted range. Which apps you connect and what permissions you have open limit what the agent can do.

marks.span: Check the result: Correct the plan because the format of one file is different.
marks.note: This is the point where the agent sees the results and revises the plan for itself. This repetition allows multiple steps to be handled with a single instruction.

marks.span: Confirmation request: Login is required and waits for a response from the user.
marks.note: Intervention during execution. When verification or login is required, the agent stops and waits for a human response. A person may change direction or stop working.

marks.span: Delivery: A person checks the final numbers and distributes them.
marks.note: It's an intervention after it's over. A person checks the results and decides whether to share them or not. This verification is especially important because agents using the app as a data source may have access to sensitive information.

screens.outro: Now that we have identified the intervention points, let's apply them to our monthly settlement reporting task.

screens.title: Commentary: Breaking down the monthly balance reporting task into steps
screens.lead: The instructor will break down the monthly financial reporting task into steps and explain who will be in charge. Select the arrow to move on.

steps.title: 1. Collect last month’s settlement file: Agent
steps.body: This involves finding and reading a file at a specified location. The rules are clear and the results are easy to review, so agents call the tool and take care of it. It is safer to limit the reading location to a specified folder.

steps.title: 2. Calculating totals by item and organizing tables: Agent
steps.body: The task of totaling each item and organizing it into a table is left to the agent as the standards are fixed. The resulting table is easy to check against the original totals, so review costs are small.

steps.title: 3. Displaying an amount that is significantly different from usual: displayed by the agent, judged by the person
steps.body: Agents may find and display amounts that are significantly different from previous months. However, someone who knows the circumstances must decide whether the amount is a mistake or a normal change. At this stage, the agent stops and hands the seat over to a human.

steps.title: 4. Drafting the report: Agent
steps.body: It is up to the agent to draft a report based on the confirmed numbers. A draft is a draft after all and remains undistributed.

steps.title: 5. Verification and distribution of final numbers: people
steps.body: Final numbers carry responsibility, and once deployed they are difficult to return. Therefore, this step is handled by humans. In the entire flow, humans have two roles: 3 judgments and 5 confirmations, and the rest is handled by agents.

screens.outro: Now that we have divided the steps, let us summarize the criteria for dividing the section into entrusted parts.

screens.title: Commentary: Criteria for dividing the section to be entrusted
screens.lead: As you select each standard, the instructor's commentary unfolds. Please read it in connection with the previous monthly settlement example.

items.prompt: Criterion 1: Are the rules clear and results easy to review?
items.answer: If so, I'll leave it to you. This includes collecting settlement files and calculating totals. If the rules can be written down and the results are easy to compare to the original, it will be easy to notice if the agent is wrong.

items.prompt: Criterion 2: Is the decision responsible or difficult to reverse?
items.answer: Then people do it. This includes determining the reason for the abnormal amount and confirming and distributing the final number. This standard is the reason why numbers 3 and 5 in the case are for people.

items.prompt: Criteria 3: Can I entrust everything from the beginning?
items.answer: First, start by checking the operation with a sample request in Preview. As evidence builds that the results are trustworthy, the scope of entrustment is gradually expanded. Conversely, if a problem arises, you can narrow the scope again.

items.prompt: What is easy to miss when applying standards?
items.answer: Permission. The scope of apps and files to be used by agents is determined by humans. When deciding on the section to be entrusted, the scope within which the agent can access it must also be narrowly determined. Agents who use the app as a data source need to be especially careful as they may have access to sensitive information.

screens.outro: Lastly, I will summarize the contents of this class.

screens.title: Decide which section to leave to the agent
screens.lead: We will organize the contents so far into one judgment standard.

paragraphs: Let's go back to the first question. When you entrust a task to an agent, the process of making a plan, calling a tool, seeing the results, and revising the plan is repeated. The reason I was anxious about only seeing the results was because I couldn't see this repetitive process.

Human intervention comes in three places: Before starting, decide on your goals, tools, and scope of approach. While running, the agent stops and responds when asked for confirmation. After finishing, check the results and decide whether to share them.

The section to be entrusted is one where the rules are clear and easy to review, while the section to be handled by a person is one where responsibility comes and is difficult to reverse. By this standard, in the case of monthly settlement, the agent was responsible for collection, calculation, and drafting, and the person was responsible for judgment and final confirmation of abnormal amounts.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: Agents iterate on plans, tools, and results. Sections with clear rules are left to others, and areas where responsibility is required are left to people.

checks.q: Which best describes how a workspace agent handles multi-step tasks?
options: Executes and completes the first instructions received at once.
Make a plan, use tools, see the results, and repeat the plan.
A person must manually enter all inputs at each step to proceed to the next step.
Create results using only the memory of the model without any connected tools.
checks.explain: The agent divides the goal into steps, obtains information or acts with a tool, sees the results, and repeats the process of moving to the next step.

wrong.0: The key to being an agent is repetition, looking at step-by-step results and revising the plan, which is different from completing it all at once.
wrong.2: Humans intervene before starting, when necessary during execution, and after completion, but do not provide input directly at all steps.
wrong.3: Agents call connected apps, files, and tools like search to obtain information and take action.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: Match each step of the monthly settlement reporting work with the person responsible for it.
left: Collect settlement files and organize total tables by item
Determine the reason for an amount that is significantly different from usual
Confirmation and distribution of final numbers
right: A person is in charge. There is responsibility for the results and it is difficult to reverse them.
Agent handles it as a tool
The agent displays the information, but the reason is determined by a person.
checks.explain: The collection and calculation with clear rules are handled by the agent, and since the judgment is responsible, the interpretation of the amount and the final confirmation and distribution are handled by the person.
checks.intro: Try to organize the concepts and explanations by pairing them. Results are not recorded.

glossary.def: An agent that creates, shares, and executes on schedule for repetitive tasks within your organization.
It is the process of dividing a goal into steps, performing them one by one, and revising the plan based on the results.
The agent calls up connected apps, files, or tools such as search to obtain information or take action.
This is the point where the agent stops or hands over the results for a human to check and decide. Enter before starting, during execution, and after completion.

misconceptions.myth: The agent answers once and it's over.
misconceptions.fact: Agents work through several iterations of planning, calling tools, and checking results. We sometimes change our plans after seeing the results.

misconceptions.myth: Once you leave it in, there is no need for anyone to see it.
misconceptions.fact: Sections that are difficult to reverse or involve liability must be checked by a person. Agents also stop and ask for human confirmation when necessary.
Role-based access control is enforced, so users can only view and run agents they have permission to access.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Agents work by iterating through plans, tools, and results.
The points of human intervention are before, during, and after the start.
I leave it to sections where the rules are clear and easy to review.
Sections that require responsibility or are difficult to reverse are handled by humans.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What section of my work will the agent take over and which section will I leave behind?
